description: A chief run today executes under WHATEVER credentials the invoking shell happens to carry: the provider subprocess (`_run_provider` in `engine/agent.sh`) inherits the driver's environment wholesale, and there is no documented, tested seam to start a run UNDER A DESIGNATED ACCOUNT (e.g. a different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`/OAuth home or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for claude, or the analogous credential env of devin/opencode/amp). chief-cloud's `91-account-pooling-and-capacity-balancing` needs exactly this runner-side prerequisite — its daemon balances runs across an operator-configured account pool by shelling out to `chief`, and chief-cloud's CLAUDE.md places runner changes HERE, in chief. This tasklist adds a per-run credential-env pass-through: an operator (or a parent process like chief-cloud's daemon) designates a credential env file for the run, chief applies it around the provider invocation ONLY, and secrets never land in logs, the run registry, liveliness records, or state. Additive: with no designation the inherited-environment behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged. Scope: `bin/chief` (flag), `engine/driver.sh` (plumb-through), `engine/agent.sh` (apply at `_run_provider`), `docs/`, `test/`; editing `engine/`/`bin/` bumps `VERSION`.

userStories.title: A per-run credential env designation the engine applies at the provider boundary
userStories.description: One mechanism, file-based so secret VALUES never appear on a command line or in argv: `chief run --account-env <file>` (equivalently `CHIEF_ACCOUNT_ENV_FILE=<file>`), a KEY=VALUE env file applied to the provider subprocess only.
acceptanceCriteria: `chief run --account-env <file>` (and the `CHIEF_ACCOUNT_ENV_FILE` env equivalent, usable from `.chief/config` or a headless caller) designates a KEY=VALUE credential env file for the run; the path is resolved at launch and handed through driver -> worker -> `engine/agent.sh` like the existing `CHIEF_*` plumb-throughs

The designated env is applied ONLY around the `_run_provider` invocation — the driver's own git/verify/merge phases, the verify hook, and any iteration hooks run under the normal environment — so a credential can never leak into commits or hooks that don't need it

A missing or unreadable file fails the run LOUDLY at launch (before any agent turn), never silently falling back to the inherited account; with no designation at all, behavior is unchanged (the provider inherits the environment exactly as today)
Bash 3.2 compatible; `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S error` clean; `VERSION` bumped (`test/version-bump.sh` green)

userStories.title: Secrets stay out of every observability surface
userStories.description: The seam's correctness bar is non-leakage: designation is visible, values never are.
acceptanceCriteria: Credential VALUES from the env file never appear in: the run registry (`~/.chief/runs/*.run`), liveliness records (`*.live.json`), per-iteration logs (`chief logs`), `chief ps`/`chief monitor` output, `CHIEF_VERBOSE` traces, or anything written under `.chief/state/`

What IS recorded is the designation itself (the env-file PATH and/or an operator-chosen account label), so `ps`/`monitor`/the status stream can show WHICH account a run uses without exposing its secrets
The env-file path is passed as a path and read by the engine at provider-invocation time — variable VALUES are never spliced into any command line where `ps`/argv could expose them

userStories.title: Document + hermetically test the seam as the contract chief-cloud consumes
userStories.description: Name this the runner-side account-selection contract that chief-cloud's `91-account-pooling-and-capacity-balancing` builds on, and pin it with a scripted-fake test.
acceptanceCriteria: `docs/` documents the seam (extend `docs/drivers-and-safety.md` or add a doc linked from README): the flag/env-var/file format, the provider-boundary-only application, the loud-failure rule, per-provider credential examples (claude: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; devin/opencode/amp: their documented credential envs), and an explicit note that this is the per-run account designation a multi-account pooler (chief-cloud `91`) drives — chief itself does no pooling or balancing

A hermetic test (scripted fake provider on `PATH`, temp `CHIEF_*` prefixes) asserts: a fake that echoes a designated variable proves the env REACHED the provider subprocess; the same value is absent from the run registry, live records, and logs; a bogus `--account-env` path fails the launch; and an undesignated run still passes the existing smoke path
The test joins `test/all.sh` + CI; existing `test/*.sh` still pass; README's command table gains the `--account-env` flag (keeping the `86-doc-sync-gate` invariant if it has landed)
